title: Energy, Work and Power Module 5 Lesson 1: Constant Speed Hill Work custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A car of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ ascends a distance of $80\text{ m}$ up a straight hill inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.05$, at a constant speed. The constant resistance to motion is $600\text{ N}$. Calculate the total work done by the driving force. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A cyclist of mass $75\text{ kg}$ free-wheels down a hill inclined at $4^\circ$ to the horizontal at a constant speed of $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. During a distance of $120\text{ m}$, the cyclist does no work. Calculate the work done against the resistance forces. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A sledge of mass $40\text{ kg}$ is pulled at a constant speed a distance of $25\text{ m}$ up a slope inclined at $15^\circ$ to the horizontal. The tension in the rope is parallel to the slope. The total work done by the tension is $3500\text{ J}$. Calculate the work done against friction. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A van of mass $1800\text{ kg}$ travels $200\text{ m}$ up a hill inclined at an angle $\alpha$ where $\sin\alpha = 0.04$ at a constant speed. The work done by the driving force over this distance is $194\text{ kJ}$. Find the magnitude of the constant resistance to motion. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A loaded lorry of mass $12000\text{ kg}$ descends a hill inclined at an angle $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.06$ at a constant speed. In travelling a distance of $150\text{ m}$, the resistance to motion does $180\text{ kJ}$ of work. The engine does no work, and the brakes are applied. Calculate the work done by the braking force. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A tractor of mass $3500\text{ kg}$ climbs a slope inclined at an angle $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.08$ at a constant speed. The resistance to motion is $700\text{ N}$. The engine performs $350\text{ kJ}$ of work. Calculate the distance the tractor travels up the slope. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.prompt: A car of mass $1500\text{ kg}$ travels a distance of $250\text{ m}$ up a hill inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = 0.04$, at a constant speed of $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. A constant resistance to motion of magnitude $800\text{ N}$ acts on the car. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the increase in gravitational potential energy of the car, the work done against the resistance force, and the total work done by the driving force of the engine.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the time taken to travel this distance and the power developed by the engine in $\text{kW}$.

questions.prompt: A box of mass $50\text{ kg}$ is pulled a distance of $40\text{ m}$ up a rough inclined plane at a constant speed by a cable parallel to the plane. The plane is inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.28$ and $\cos\theta = 0.96$. The coefficient of friction between the box and the plane is $\mu = 0.15$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the frictional force acting on the box and the work done against friction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the gain in potential energy and hence determine the tension in the cable.

questions.prompt: A car of mass $M\text{ kg}$ is towing a trailer of mass $400\text{ kg}$ down a straight hill inclined at $3^\circ$ to the horizontal at a constant speed. There are constant resistance forces on both the car and the trailer. The total work done against resistance forces in a distance of $80\text{ m}$ is $50200\text{ J}$. The engine of the car does no work and the towbar is light and rigid. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Using the work-energy principle, calculate the total mass of the car and trailer, and find the value of $M$ to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The resistance force on the trailer is $250\text{ N}$. Find the tension or thrust in the towbar between the car and the trailer.

questions.prompt: An electric conveyor ramp is used to lift ore from a mine at a constant speed of $2.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The ramp is inclined at an angle $\alpha$ where $\sin\alpha = 0.12$. The conveyor carries ore of total mass $8000\text{ kg}$ on its surface at any given moment against a constant frictional resistance of $4000\text{ N}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Over a distance of $60\text{ m}$ along the ramp, calculate the work done against gravity, the work done against friction, and the total work done by the motor driving the conveyor.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the time taken to move this distance, the power output of the conveyor motor in $\text{kW}$, and the efficiency of the motor given that it consumes $40\text{ kW}$ of electrical power.

questions.prompt: A lorry of mass $9000\text{ kg}$ ascends a straight incline of length $500\text{ m}$ inclined at an angle $\theta$ where $\sin\theta = 0.05$ at a constant speed of $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The constant resistance to motion is $1500\text{ N}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the engine during the ascent and the power developed by the engine in $\text{kW}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The lorry now descends the same $500\text{ m}$ incline at a constant speed of $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The resistance to motion remains $1500\text{ N}$. The engine does no work and the brakes are applied. Calculate the work done by the braking force, the average braking force, and the rate at which heat is generated by the brakes in $\text{kW}$.

questions.prompt: An articulated hauler of mass $15000\text{ kg}$ is connected to a dump trailer of mass $10000\text{ kg}$ by a rigid horizontal towbar. The hauler moves at a constant speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up a quarry ramp inclined at an angle $\alpha$ where $\sin\alpha = 0.08$. The resistance to motion is $2400\text{ N}$ on the hauler and $1600\text{ N}$ on the trailer. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: In climbing a distance of $120\text{ m}$ along the ramp, calculate the total gain in potential energy of the combination, the total work done against resistance, the work done by the hauler's engine, and the power output of the engine in $\text{kW}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the towbar between the hauler and trailer during this climb, find the work done by the towbar on the trailer over the $120\text{ m}$, and verify that this equals the trailer's gain in potential energy plus the work done against the trailer's resistance.

questions.prompt: A cable-driven mountain funicular carriage of mass $6000\text{ kg}$ is pulled up a track $PQ$ of length $300\text{ m}$ inclined at $12^\circ$ to the horizontal at a constant speed of $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. A constant frictional resistance of $1800\text{ N}$ opposes the motion. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the cable during the ascent, the work done by the cable in pulling the carriage from $P$ to $Q$, and the average power developed by the cable winch in $\text{kW}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: On the return descent from $Q$ to $P$, the carriage descends at the same constant speed of $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, but passengers of total mass $1500\text{ kg}$ board at $Q$ (increasing total mass to $7500\text{ kg}$). The resistance to motion remains $1800\text{ N}$. The cable must now restrain the carriage to maintain constant speed. Calculate the braking tension in the cable during the descent, the work done on the winch by the restraining cable over the $300\text{ m}$, and the power regenerated or dissipated by the winch in $\text{kW}$.
